headline: Algorithms enumerate structured paths and blocks in graph and genealogical sequence data
label: Combinatorial Path And Block Enumeration
summary: Combinatorial formulations with stated complexity are emerging for path and block inference across graph, genealogical, and synteny representations.
synthesis: Three preprints share a combinatorial emphasis: enumerating or deriving structured paths and blocks from sequence-level inputs rather than reporting new biological findings. The pangenome study enumerates all maximal paths in a graph aligning with a given chain of sequences, allowing user-specified maximal gaps. The gene-tree study links genetic tree sequences to genealogical pedigree trees by enumerating consistent ancestry paths, demonstrated on the BALSAC Quebec dataset. The synteny study derives collinear blocks by compacting sequence elements without breakpoints, treating the underlying problems as NP-hard and giving a linear-time algorithm. What is new is explicit path and block formulations with stated complexity, applied across graph, genealogical, and synteny representations. Evidence is limited to algorithmic descriptions in preprints.
